read.passage: When Abdullah joined his school's discussion club, he thought the goal was to win every argument. In his first meeting, he talked over everyone and called other people's ideas 'useless'. Afterwards, the club leader, an older student, took him aside. 'What makes a good speaker,' he said, 'isn't how loudly you talk. It's how well you listen.' Over the next few weeks, Abdullah practised softening his opinions with phrases like 'I'm not entirely sure that …' and inviting quieter members to speak. He also learnt to judge ideas fairly by looking at their strengths before their drawbacks. By the end of the term, the members had chosen him as their new chairperson, something he would never have imagined on his first day.

options: He invited quiet members to speak.

options: The club closed for the summer.
